newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BA opens seven mln rand S.Africa cargo unit.
newsitem.headline: BA opens seven mln rand S.Africa cargo unit.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo (BAWC) has opened a seven million rand facility at Johannesburg International Airport to cope with the growth in air cargo between South Africa and the UK.

Opening the facility on Tuesday, Kevin Hatton, managing director of BAWC, said exports, particularly fresh produce which accounted for over 60 percent of cargo carried to the UK, had increased steadily since 1995.

He said the previous facility had been unable to cope with the projected growth and larger, better-equipped premises and more streamlined procedures were required. The new centre would soon be equipped with refrigeration facilities.
"This is the first time in our 65-year history in South Africa that we have had our own dedicated facility...Efficiency has improved since we moved premises in early December," Hatton said.

Hatton said the new cargo centre was BAWC's first to introduce a handling agreement which operates as a type of licensed franchise. Cargo Service Centre, a subsidiary of KLM Dutch Airline NV, would provide a full freight handling and sales support service on behalf of BAWC.
Hatton said the franchise concept was being extended to other stations and BAWC aimed to replace all handling agreements throughout Africa with the new arrangement.
BAWC offers 17 flights a week between South Africa and the United Kingdom.
Other than fresh produce, the remaining 40 percent of traffic comprises general cargo, which ranges from machinery to bullion.
